writeup: TIC 188173846 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 9.8940 days. The primary eclipse produces an 8.65% dimming in the TESS photometry, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 7.2 sigma significance near orbital phase 0.46. Automated analysis identified this system with a BLS signal-to-noise ratio of 63.0, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 7.0, though the centroid offset measured 2.7 arcsec from the target location. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel detection. The machine-learning screening score of 0.37 suggests moderate confidence that this represents a genuine astrophysical source rather than an instrumental artifact.
